activity_label.en: The state of play of advancing EU-Africa trade and investment relations (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Brando Benifei, on behalf of the Group S&D.

Madam President, Commissioner, a few months ago, my political group, which I represent here in the debate, the Socialists and Democrats, made ten commitments for a new relationship between Europe and Africa: Rise with Africa.

The message is clear: Africa is not a land of conquest, a mere recipient of aid or a market to enter. It is also a political, economic and social partner with its own priorities, ambitions and solutions.

This must also apply to our trade policy. Trade and investment must create shared value, support industrialisation, decent jobs and value chains where African economies can retain a larger share of the wealth they produce. That is why I mini-deals and i Clean Trade and Investment Partnerships must ensure clarity and transparency. The European Parliament must be properly involved in their negotiation, conclusion and implementation, ensuring democratic scrutiny commensurate with their importance.

Moreover, as I pointed out in my parliamentary work with the report on artificial intelligence and trade, digital must not create new dependencies. We need to invest in local infrastructure, skills and capabilities, in a close partnership with the European Union, promoting open and ethical systems.

The success of our trade policy is measured not only by how much we export, but also by how much we contribute to creating opportunities, capacity and growth, which can bring benefits for all. Thus, in this way, Europe and Africa can grow together.

activity_label.en: Effective measures to protect and empower children in the digital world (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D).

Madam President, when you ask a child today who he talks to when he is sad, one in two will tell you with a chatbot, with a machine. And it's not hard to understand why.

For many children, artificial intelligence is becoming the perfect confidant, always available, never judges and always gives you the reason. But here's the problem, what looks like companionship becomes slavery, because that listening comes at a price: emotional dependence, isolation and a mind that gets used to not thinking for itself. Our children cannot grow up learning that a machine is their best confidant.

Faced with this reality, we welcome the EU KIDS ACT that obliges chatbots and artificial intelligence colleagues to guarantee the highest levels of security and privacy for children under eighteen and also a digital minimum age, and prohibits addictive designs for minors. We have to regulate at European level and this goes beyond AI, also social networks and also video games, because we cannot ask our children to learn to set limits while the technologies themselves are designed not to have them.

So we need an emergency brake for our children, but also a Digital Fairness Act that combats addictive designs for adults. We are asked to do so by our families and also by an entire generation.
